text:
alex: Anyone else seeing Console really slow on /console/routing-policies after today's deploy? Charts hang for ~6-8s when navigating. :eyes:
priya: Yep — I just repro'd. Full page load ~4.5s, SPA nav to that route ~3-4s. Looks like JS parse + long tasks on main thread.
tj: I ran bundle-analyzer quickly — the new metrics-widget change pulled in d3 + polyfills. vendor.metrics chunk jumped ~420KB gzipped.
priya: Oof. Which PR added it?
tj: PR #4271 — it switched us to the shared metrics-widget package and enabled dynamic polyfills. Command I ran:
```
npx webpack-bundle-analyzer dist/stats.json --port 8888
// top entries: vendor~metrics.js 420KB, main.js 150KB, vendors~ui 300KB
```
kavi: Datadog RUM shows a 2-3s long task right after firstPaint on that route; flame chart points to parsing/executing vendor.metrics. Also a spike in GC while parsing.
alex: Quick check: fetching the asset headers for vendor.metrics shows weird cache headers:
```
curl -I https://console.redwood.ai/static/js/vendor.metrics.abc123.js
HTTP/2 200
content-type: application/javascript
cache-control: no-cache, no-store
etag: "abc123"
```
priya: Whoops — these are content-hash assets, they should be immutable and cached. If the CDN served them no-cache then browsers re-parse on every nav. That would explain repeated parse cost.
tj: Strange — our S3 upload/invalidator should set Cache-Control: max-age=31536000, immutable for hashed builds. Maybe a pipeline change.
kavi: Also noticed source maps weren't uploaded for today's build (404 on *.map). If sourcemaps are missing, sourcemap parsing won't block but missing maps make debugging harder. Not related to perf but FYI.
alex: Root cause hypothesis: PR #4271 added client-side polyfills + bumped bundle; pipeline change accidentally set no-cache on hashed assets. Impact = larger parse + no caching = regressed SPA nav perf.
priya: Plan: 1) rollback the canary (only canary group) or flip the canary traffic to previous build, 2) patch pipeline to set immutable caching for hashed assets, 3) revert polyfill change or lazy-load metrics widget, 4) add CI check for Cache-Control on hashed assets + RUM guardrail.
tj: I'll prepare a small patch to lazy-load the metrics widget via dynamic import (route-level):
```
const MetricsWidget = React.lazy(() => import('../widgets/metrics'))
```
That should defer parse for non-critical routes. Also will remove useDynamicPolyfills(true) from client bootstrap.
priya: deploy-bot, canary rollback please (only canary).
deploy-bot: Rolling back canary release v2026.03.18-canary-3 -> v2026.03.17-stable. Starting rollback...
deploy-bot: Canary rollback complete. Traffic switched.
kavi: CDN team — I pushed a quick fix to the s3-uploader config to set Cache-Control for hashed files. I'll add a failing test to CI that curl -I on hashed asset must contain max-age and immutable.
alex: Great. Once rollback is live, can folks watch RUM for the next 30m? Priya, can you watch the routing-policies route perf (client-side render time + FCP)?
priya: Watching now. Initial data: last 5 SPA nav samples pre-rollback: avg render 3700ms.
(pr ~15m passes)
priya: Post-rollback samples are coming in: avg render 520ms, long tasks gone. Looks like rollback + CDN fix improved it a lot. :tada:
tj: I'll open the PR with lazy-load + small polyfill change and include the bundle-analyzer before/after.
kavi: I'll land the CDN test and add a dev-doc for caching policy so we don't regress again.
alex: Thanks everyone. Action items: tj (lazy-load PR + remove polyfill), kavi (CDN fix + CI test), priya (monitoring + add RUM alerts for >1s route render), and I'll add a follow-up to the rollout runbook about checking cache headers after deploy.
priya: Added owners to the incident thread and updated on-call notes. :thumbsup:
